day_shape: 93 items: CENTCOM resumes Iran naval blockade with 20+ warships and fresh strikes, Trump threatens power-plant strikes next week, State Dept targets Shamkhani shipping network, FCDO summons Iran chargé over IRGC-QF proxy attacks, IRGC claims strikes on US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan.

threads.label: US blockade and strikes on Iran
threads.summary: CENTCOM announced it resumed the naval blockade of Iranian ports at 4pm ET with over 20 warships and launched a further round of strikes to degrade capabilities used against Hormuz shipping. Trump told Fox News the US would strike Iranian power plants and bridges next week, and Times of Israel published footage of first operational US use of suicide drone boats at Bandar Abbas.

threads.label: IRGC claims strikes on Gulf US bases
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB claimed IRGC strikes destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre in Bahrain, a Patriot complex and Mars launch site in Kuwait, and F-15/F-16/F-35 and MQ-9 assets at Al-Azraq base in Jordan. IRIB also reported an American missile strike on Bampour garrison in Iranshahr killed seven Iranian army personnel, and reported an attack on a Hoveyzeh grain silo.

threads.label: Hormuz sanctions, tolls and shipping
threads.summary: The State Department announced action against the illicit shipping network of designated Iranian Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, and Treasury issued a general license permitting Hormuz wind-down operations until 12 September. Jerusalem Post reported nine of 11 vessels transiting Hormuz on Tuesday used the Iranian route, and Iran International said Trump's short-lived 20% toll proposal was seized on by Tehran.

threads.label: UK and European diplomatic action
threads.summary: The FCDO summoned Iran's Chargé d'Affaires in London over the IRGC Quds Force's role in directing proxy attacks across Europe, confirmed by a Jerusalem Post dispatch. Jerusalem Post also reported several other countries summoned their Iranian ambassadors following the Hormuz strikes.

threads.label: Regional diplomacy and Gulf posture
threads.summary: Rubio met Jordanian FM Safadi and condemned Iranian attacks on shipping, while the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2826 extending Houthi Red Sea reporting for six months to 15 January 2027. The UAE released 55 Iranian fishermen and Trump said Gulf states should reimburse the US for wartime protection.

threads.label: Khamenei commemoration cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a message from Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei vowing not to abandon the "criminal aggressors," alongside photo and audio coverage of the commemoration for the slain leader at Imam Khomeini Prayer Ground on 23 Tir. Ayatollah Seyyed Mustafa Khamenei told the ceremony that patience was compatible with vengeance.

threads.label: Israel: espionage case, Iran plot report, Gaza strike
threads.summary: An Israeli military court sentenced an IDF conscript to five years for spying for Iran throughout 2025, and Haifa municipality said a man wounded by an Iranian ballistic missile in April's Operation Roaring Lion had died. The Times of Israel cited a New York Times report on an alleged multi-year Israeli effort to reinstall Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, and the IDF said it killed Hamas Jabalia battalion security chief Mohammed Marwan Salem.

events.title: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
events.summary: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
